editor_note: All six rewritten entries (9, 44, 65, 67, 68, 69) keep the meaning of the English: the error codes 4710/4712, the [0, 3] range, the off/weak/medium/strong to 0–3 mapping, the unchanged default of 3 and the binary-or-bounded-integer rule all match. The problems are two terminology inconsistencies with the rest of the page. The rewritten entries 9 and 68 call the generic "the function" "die Function", while entries 7, 15, 32 and 33 say "die Funktion". Entry 67 renders "preprocessing" as "Vorverarbeitung", while entries 16, 17 and 29 use "Preprocessing" throughout. Neither would mislead a learner.

examples.source: The function solves discrete problems only.
examples.translation: Die Function löst nur diskrete Probleme.
examples.suggested: Die Funktion löst nur diskrete Probleme.
examples.why: The rest of the page uses 'Funktion' for the generic lowercase 'the function' (entries 7, 15, 32, 33). Only the product name 'Qiskit Function' must stay in English. Entry 68 has the same split ('den die Function einreicht').

examples.source: The field is `None` when the problem was solved during preprocessing and no circuit was run
examples.translation: Das Feld ist `None`, wenn das Problem während der Vorverarbeitung gelöst wurde
examples.suggested: Das Feld ist `None`, wenn das Problem während des Preprocessings gelöst wurde
examples.why: Elsewhere on this page 'preprocessing' is consistently 'Preprocessing' (the **Preprocessing** workflow step, 'Graph-Preprocessing', 'im Preprocessing'). Here the changelog refers to that same step, so it should use the same term.

editor_note: Entry 28 keeps the full meaning with no drift: the QPU time is still "minimal und nahezu konstant", the reason "da nur eine Runde von QAOA … verwendet wird" is preserved, and "auf einer CPU ermittelten Circuit-Parametern" carries the CPU qualifier. "Eine Runde von QAOA" is a slight calque, but it matches entry [15], so it is defensible.

The rewritten entries 40, 41 and 44 keep the meaning of the English. The figures (below 10 % at width 9 with 10 qubits, Orbit at 80–90 %, about 15 % near width 60, N = 50 with 51 qubits) and the closing caveat about calibration and settings are all intact. There are two small wording problems. The heading in entry 40, "auf größere Größen skalieren", repeats "Größe" and sounds clumsy. Entries 41 and 44 call raw execution "Rohausführung" and "rohe Erfolgswahrscheinlichkeit", but the nearby entries 38, 39 and 50 say "Raw-Ausführung" and "Raw-Modus", and the benchmark table says "unverändert", so the same idea now has three German names.

examples.why: "größere Größen" says the same thing twice and reads like a word-for-word translation. A native technical writer would say "Problemgrößen" or "mehr Qubits".

examples.source: compare raw execution with Orbit configurations ... raw success probability falls below 10%
examples.translation: vergleichen die Rohausführung mit Orbit-Konfigurationen ... fällt die rohe Erfolgswahrscheinlichkeit
examples.suggested: vergleichen die Raw-Ausführung mit Orbit-Konfigurationen ... fällt die Erfolgswahrscheinlichkeit ohne Orbit (Raw)
examples.why: Entries 38, 39 and 50 say "Raw-Ausführung" and "Raw-Modus" for the same thing, so "Roh-" brings in a third name for one concept. "rohe Erfolgswahrscheinlichkeit" also sounds odd in German.

examples.source: comparing raw execution with Orbit defaults in a single job
examples.translation: und vergleicht die Rohausführung mit den Orbit-Standardeinstellungen in einem einzigen Job
examples.suggested: und vergleicht die Raw-Ausführung mit den Orbit-Standardeinstellungen in einem einzigen Job
examples.why: Use the same word for raw execution as entry 38 ("Raw-Ausführung"), which describes this exact example.

editor_note: Delta read of entries 72 and 73 only, covering naturalness (check 1) and semantic drift (check 3). Neither entry misleads. Entry 72 keeps the control and target roles (Q as Steuer-Qubit, Alice's qubit as Ziel-Qubit) and the order "CNOT, then Hadamard on Q", and the math in entry 73 is unchanged. Its prose sentence "gruppieren wir die obigen Terme nach den möglichen Messergebnissen der Qubits A und Q" is faithful. The "möglichen" it adds is harmless. One naturalness slip remains: entry 72 says "appliziert anschließend ein Hadamard-Gate auf Q". "Applizieren" is a stiff anglicism for applying a gate, and the same sentence already uses "wendet … an", the usual verb found elsewhere on the page.

examples.line_approx: Alice verschränkt die Qubits A und Q
examples.source: then applies a Hadamard gate to Q
examples.translation: und appliziert anschließend ein Hadamard-Gate auf Q
examples.suggested: Alice wendet nun ein CNOT-Gate mit Q als Steuer-Qubit und ihrem eigenen Qubit als Ziel-Qubit an und führt anschließend ein Hadamard-Gate auf Q aus.
examples.why: German quantum-computing writers almost never say 'applizieren' for a gate. It reads like a calque of 'apply'. The page otherwise uses 'anwenden', and 'ausführen' avoids repeating that verb within one sentence.

editor_note: Entries 53 and 78 keep the English meaning ("lege die Option `seed_transpiler` fest", "mehrere entartete Optima") and need no changes. Entry 87 has two small problems that don't mislead. First, "constrained binary optimization problem" becomes "eingeschränktes binäres Optimierungsproblem", which is a calque and clashes with the established "mit Nebenbedingungen" used in entries 7 and 17. Second, "detailed walkthrough of all function features" becomes "detaillierte Übersicht über alle Funktionen der Function": "Übersicht" loses the step-by-step sense of "walkthrough", and "Funktionen der Function" is a clumsy repetition.

examples.source: on your own constrained binary optimization problem
examples.translation: für dein eigenes eingeschränktes binäres Optimierungsproblem
examples.suggested: an deinem eigenen binären Optimierungsproblem mit Nebenbedingungen
examples.why: 'eingeschränkt' is a calque of 'constrained'. The rest of the file uses 'mit Nebenbedingungen' (entries 7, 17), so this rendering is inconsistent.

examples.source: for a detailed walkthrough of all function features
examples.translation: eine detaillierte Übersicht über alle Funktionen der Function
examples.suggested: eine ausführliche Schritt-für-Schritt-Erklärung aller Features der Function
examples.why: 'Funktionen der Function' is an awkward repetition, and 'Übersicht' (overview) flattens 'walkthrough'.

editor_note: Entry 60 keeps the meaning of the English and keeps "Qiskit Function" in English, as house style requires. The problem is word order. The apposition "einer Qiskit Function von Quantum Elements" comes after the final infinitive "benchmarken", so it is cut off from "Orbit", the word it describes, and reads like a calque. A native writer would put the apposition right after "Orbit" and end the sentence with the verb. "Prozessgüte" is an acceptable rendering of "process fidelity", but "Prozessfidelität" is the more common term in the German QC literature.

examples.source: Benchmark QFT process fidelity with Orbit, a Qiskit Function by Quantum Elements
examples.translation: QFT-Prozessgüte mit Orbit benchmarken, einer Qiskit Function von Quantum Elements
examples.suggested: QFT-Prozessfidelität mit Orbit, einer Qiskit Function von Quantum Elements, benchmarken
examples.why: The apposition comes after the final verb, so it is cut off from "Orbit" and reads like a calque of the English word order. Putting it right after "Orbit" and the verb at the end is the natural German order.

editor_note: Entry 12 is faithful and reads naturally. It keeps the triangle-frustration example and the all-to-all cause ("Da im SK-Modell jeder Spin mit jedem anderen Spin wechselwirkt"), and renders "compounded globally, leading to a web of conflicting constraints" as "global verstärkt, was zu einem Geflecht widersprüchlicher Bedingungen führt".

None of the 23 rewritten entries changes the meaning, so nothing here would mislead a learner. The numbers (921.600 Shots, 300 PUBs, 60 PUBs per N), the conditions in entry 17 (O(n^2) vs O(n), "Sofern ... fehlerarm genug") and the 6073 remedies in entries 32 and 67 all match the English. The remaining issues are about wording. "Child job" is translated two ways: as half-English "child Job(s)" in entries 5 and 11, and as "untergeordneter Job" in entries 4, 32, 49 and 51. Entries 0 and 10 also use a broken shortened compound, "unitäre Roh-, dynamische Roh- und Orbit-verbesserte dynamische Implementierungen/Varianten". The "Roh-" parts need a compound noun like "Rohimplementierungen" at the end, but the last item is not one.

examples.source: partitioning circuit sizes across three Runtime Batch child jobs
examples.translation: indem es die Circuit-Größen auf drei Runtime Batch child Jobs aufteilt
examples.suggested: indem es die Circuit-Größen auf drei untergeordnete Jobs des Runtime Batch aufteilt
examples.why: The half-English 'child Jobs' does not match 'untergeordneter Job', which entries 4, 32, 49 and 51 use for the same idea. The same split appears in entry 11 ('in einem child Job').

examples.source: compare raw unitary, raw dynamic, and Orbit-enhanced dynamic implementations
examples.translation: vergleiche unitäre Roh-, dynamische Roh- und Orbit-verbesserte dynamische Implementierungen
examples.suggested: vergleiche rohe unitäre, rohe dynamische und Orbit-verbesserte dynamische Implementierungen
examples.why: The shortened 'Roh-' forms need a compound noun such as 'Rohimplementierungen' at the end, but the last item is 'Orbit-verbesserte dynamische Implementierungen'. That makes the phrase ungrammatical and hard to read. Entry 10 has the same structure with 'Varianten'.

examples.source: Compare raw unitary, raw dynamic, and Orbit-enhanced dynamic QFT process-fidelity estimates
examples.translation: Vergleiche Schätzungen der QFT-Prozessfidelity für unitäre Roh-, dynamische Roh- und Orbit-verbesserte dynamische Varianten
examples.suggested: Vergleiche Schätzungen der QFT-Prozessfidelity für die rohe unitäre, die rohe dynamische und die Orbit-verbesserte dynamische Variante
examples.why: Same broken shortened compound as in entry 0. It reads like a calque in a learning outcome.
